1.title: Exam Technique and Final Review
1.text: Welcome to Module fifteen: Exam Technique and Final Review. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do seven things. The time budget. The routine for every question. Domain checklists. Pairs the exam likes to confuse. Common traps. The final week. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Scope: All three domains. Exam format: forty-five minutes; a score of seven hundred on a scale of one to one thousand passes. Validated against: the official A Z nine hundred study guide, current skills measured.

1.title: The time budget
1.text: The time budget. The assessment is forty-five minutes. The number of questions is not given on the pages this course was built from, so check the exam page and divide the time by the count. First pass. About one minute per question: answer what you know, mark the rest. Second pass. Return to marked questions with the time left. Last minutes. Make sure no question is left empty.

1.title: The time budget, continued
1.text: The time budget. The figure shows this: A forty-five-minute plan: first pass, marked questions, final check.

1.title: The time budget, continued
1.text: The time budget. Note. Some exams contain sections that cannot be reviewed after you move on. Read the on-screen instructions before you start each section.

1.title: The routine for every question
1.text: The routine for every question. Read the last sentence first: what is being asked (which service, model, benefit, tool)? Find the key need: "no servers to manage", "keep data in the country", "private connection", "enforce a rule", "prevent deletion". Name the category (compute, storage, networking, identity, governance, monitoring, cost) and drop options from other categories. Choose the most specific match for the need. Mark and move on if two options remain after a minute.

1.title: Cloud concepts (25–30%)
1.text: Cloud concepts (twenty-five to thirty percent). Shared responsibility: always the customer's data, devices, accounts and identities. Public, private and hybrid, with a use case for each. Consumption-based model; cap ex versus op ex; reservations. Serverless equals no server management, pay for execution. Benefits: high availability, scalability (up or out), reliability, predictability, security, governance, manageability. I A A S, pass, sass and who manages what.

1.title: Azure architecture and services (35–40%)
1.text: Azure architecture and services (thirty-five to forty percent). Regions, region pairs, sovereign regions, availability zones, datacenters. Hierarchy: management group to subscription to resource group to resource. Compute: V Ms, scale sets, availability sets, Azure Virtual Desktop, containers (A C I, A K S), Functions, App Service. Networking: V net, subnet, peering, Azure D N S, V P N (virtual private network) Gateway versus Express Route, public versus private endpoint. Storage: Blob, Files, Queue, Table, Disk; tiers; L R S (locally redundant storage), Z R S (zone-redundant storage), G R S (geo-redundant storage), G Z R S (geo-zone-redundant storage); Az Copy, Storage Explorer, File Sync; Azure Migrate, Data Box. Identity: Entra I D, Entra Domain Services, S S O, M F A, passwordless, external identities, Conditional Access, R B A C. Security: Zero Trust, defense in depth, Defender for Cloud.

1.title: Management and governance (30–35%)
1.text: Management and governance (thirty to thirty-five percent). Cost factors, pricing calculator, Cost Management, tags. Purview, Azure Policy, resource locks. Portal, Cloud Shell, C L I, Power Shell, Azure Arc, I A C, A R M (Azure Resource Manager) and templates. Advisor, Service Health, Azure Monitor (Log Analytics, alerts, Application Insights).

1.title: Pairs the exam likes to confuse
1.text: Pairs the exam likes to confuse. V P N Gateway versus Express Route. encrypted over the internet versus private dedicated line. Scale set versus availability set. identical autoscaling V Ms versus fault and update domains. Zones versus region pair. protect a datacenter failure versus a regional disaster. Azure Policy versus R B A C. what configuration is allowed versus who can act. Policy versus locks. enforce rules versus prevent delete or change. Advisor versus Service Health. improve my setup versus Azure's own problems. Advisor versus Defender for Cloud. general recommendations versus security posture and threats.

1.title: Pairs the exam likes to confuse, continued
1.text: Pairs the exam likes to confuse. Entra I D versus Entra Domain Services. cloud identity versus managed domain (L D A P, Kerberos, group policy). Pricing calculator versus Cost Management. estimate a plan versus analyze what you spend. A C I versus A K S. quick single containers versus orchestration. Authentication versus authorization. who you are versus what you may do. Blob versus Files. objects versus S M B (Server Message Block) slash N F S (Network File System) file shares. Public versus private endpoint. public I P versus private I P from your V net. I A A S versus pass. you patch the O S versus the provider does.

1.title: Common traps
1.text: Common traps. "The provider is compliant, so I am." Compliance is shared. Tags are inherited. Not by default. Cheaper storage tier costs less to read. The opposite: cooler tiers cost more to access. Zones work in every region. Not every region has zones. A read-only lock only stops deleting. It stops modifying as well; the delete lock stops deleting only. Azure D N S sells domain names. It hosts D N S records. V P N Gateway avoids the internet. It encrypts traffic over the internet. Serverless has no servers. The provider runs them. Old names: Azure Active Directory equals Microsoft Entra I D.

1.title: The final week
1.text: The final week. seven to five. Re-read one module per day with the Quick Reference Card; answer its recall questions from memory. four to three. Do the comparison pairs table and the traps list out loud. two. Answer the practice questions in all modules again; note every miss. one. Light review of the cards; check the exam time, I D and online or test center rules; rest.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. Fabrikam Outdoors wants to run a Windows server it fully controls, and it will patch the operating system itself. Which service type is this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: I A A S. Controlling and patching the O S is I A A S.

2.title: Practice Question 2
2.text: Question two. Which Azure feature protects a workload from the failure of one datacenter inside a region? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Availability zones. Availability zones are separate locations inside a region.

2.title: Practice Question 3
2.text: Question three. A company needs a private, dedicated connection to Azure that does not use the public internet. What should it use? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Express Route. Express Route is a private connection through a provider.

2.title: Practice Question 4
2.text: Question four. Which role assignment lets someone manage resources but not give access to others? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Contributor. Contributor can create and manage resources but cannot assign roles.

2.title: Practice Question 5
2.text: Question five. Which storage option has the lowest storage cost but needs hours to read? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Archive. Archive is offline and must be rehydrated.

2.title: Practice Question 6
2.text: Question six. Which tool enforces that every resource has a Cost Center tag? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Azure Policy. Azure Policy can require or add tags.

2.title: Practice Question 7
2.text: Question seven. Which tool gives personalized recommendations for reliability, security, performance, cost and operational excellence? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Azure Advisor. Advisor provides those five categories.

2.title: Practice Question 8
2.text: Question eight. A resource group holds production resources that must not be deleted by mistake. What should be applied? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: A delete lock. A delete lock on the group protects everything in it.

2.title: Practice Question 9
2.text: Question nine. Which model keeps some systems on-premises while using Azure for extra capacity? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Hybrid cloud. Hybrid combines on-premises or private with public cloud.

2.title: Practice Question 10
2.text: Question ten. An administrator wants to manage servers in another cloud from Azure with Azure Policy and tags. What fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Azure Arc. Azure Arc extends Azure management to non-Azure resources.

2.title: Practice Question 11
2.text: Question eleven. Which feature requires a second proof of identity, such as a code from a phone, in addition to a password? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Multifactor authentication. M F A requires two or more factors.

2.title: Practice Question 12
2.text: Question twelve. A team wants to estimate the cost of a planned deployment before creating it. Which tool should it use? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Azure pricing calculator. The pricing calculator estimates planned deployments.

2.title: Recall Check 1
2.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. Which three things are always the customer's responsibility? Answer: Data, devices, and accounts and identities. Question two. Order the Azure hierarchy from top to bottom. Answer: Management group, subscription, resource group, resource. Question three. Which services connect on-premises to Azure, and which one avoids the internet? Answer: V P N Gateway and Express Route; Express Route avoids the public internet.

2.title: Recall Check 2
2.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. Name the Zero Trust principles. Answer: Verify explicitly, use least-privilege access, assume breach. Question five. Which tool queries logs with K Q L? Answer: Log Analytics (in Azure Monitor). Question six. What do you read first in a question? Answer: The last sentence.

2.title: Module Recap
2.text: Here is the recap. Time: forty-five minutes; first pass, mark, second pass, no blanks. Method: last sentence, key need, drop other categories, most specific match. Domains: cloud concepts twenty-five to thirty percent; architecture and services thirty-five to forty percent; management and governance thirty to thirty-five percent. Biggest confusions: V P N versus Express Route; Policy versus R B A C versus locks; Advisor versus Service Health versus Defender. Traps: shared compliance; tags not inherited; cooler tiers cost more to read. That completes the course. Good luck with the exam.
